options: Hints to browser to create rendering layer
explanation: will-change tells browsers to prepare for changes; use sparingly (3-4 elements max) to optimize animation performance.

options: transform uses GPU, left causes reflow
explanation: transform and opacity bypass reflow/repaint (composite-only); left/top trigger layout recalculation on every frame.

options: Read (offsetWidth) forces layout, write forces reflow; repeating thrashes
explanation: Reading layout then writing forces sync reflow 100 times; batching all reads then all writes prevents thrashing.

options: Isolates element; prevents reflow affecting outside
explanation: contain: layout style paint tells browser element won't affect siblings; enables independent reflow and repaint optimization.

options: Prevents invisible text delay; shows fallback immediately
explanation: font-display: swap shows fallback while font loads, avoiding invisible text (FOIT); improves perceived performance.

question:
How does splitting CSS into multiple files impact performance?
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="main.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="theme.css">
```
options: More HTTP requests; use sparingly or bundle
explanation: More CSS files = more requests (overhead); modern builds bundle CSS; HTTP/2 helps but single file still optimal.

question:
What is the purpose of critical CSS, and when is it extracted?
```html
<style>/* Critical above-fold CSS inlined */</style>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="rest.css">
```
options: Inline above-fold CSS to unblock rendering
explanation: Critical CSS (above-fold styles) is inlined in HTML head; non-critical deferred, reducing First Contentful Paint.

question:
How do render-blocking stylesheets affect page load, and how is this mitigated?
```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> <!-- blocks rendering -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="print.css" media="print"> <!-- doesn't block -->
```
options: Parser pauses rendering until CSS loaded
Can defer non-critical CSS via media queries
explanation: CSS blocks rendering by default; media queries, async loading, or preload hints mitigate blocking.

question:
Why should selector specificity be kept low for performance?
```css
.page .section .article .paragraph .text { } /* high specificity, deep match */
.text { } /* low specificity, fast match */
```
options: Specificity affects runtime, not match time
explanation: Selector complexity has minimal impact on modern browsers; cascade and reflows matter more than selector depth.
Minification removes whitespace; tree-shaking (PurgeCSS, Tailwind) removes unused rules by analyzing HTML.
